title: folio-enrich — NER cross-validation gold-set eval
description: Deterministic (free) precision/recall/F1 for ner_cross_validation_enabled, flag OFF vs ON, over an oracle-seeded gold set; borderline cases surfaced for human verification; full-mode spend estimate queued.

sections.title: Method — deterministic (free) NER cross-validation eval
sections.body_html:
NER cross-validation (ner_cross_validation_enabled, default False) is a fully deterministic post-LLM pass: it boosts/penalizes annotation confidence using spaCy NER labels vs. a per-ontology branch affinity map, rejecting spans that fall below 0.20. Running the pipeline with llm=None gives a reproducible, /bin/bash ruler→NER→reconcile→resolve path that still exercises the flag. This pack reports that free comparison; the authoritative full-pipeline (LLM-sourced) comparison is spend-gated and queued to the QA portal.

Gold: 52 scored (oracle-verified) + 94 borderline (awaiting human verification), across 6 demo docs. Precision/recall are span-restricted over the labelled spans (correct for a sampled gold).

Recommendation: HOLD_no_f1_gain. On the unambiguous deterministic set NER cross-validation is recall-safe — it was free to reject any of the 52 scored spans and rejected none — but shows no F1 gain there. Its discriminating signal lives in the borderline + LLM-sourced concepts, which the free tier does not cover. Default stays False pending the spend-gated run.

sections.title: Spend estimate — authoritative full-mode run (queued)
sections.body_html: The authoritative flip signal needs the LLM candidate stages ON. Because the NER flag only changes deterministic reconciliation, that is one LLM pass per doc + a free replay OFF/ON. Token-grounded estimate over the 6 gold docs (google/gemini-3-flash-preview): ~114K input + 43K output tokens → /bin/bash.03–/bin/bash.14 (range = flash-class price assumption, the one figure to confirm). Queued to the QA portal (briefs/qa/pending-questions.jsonl) per TODAY policy — not run.
